csat-english-blank-inference-100.summary: 빈칸 추론 한 유형만으로 구성되는 방식을 보여 줍니다. 문항마다 빈칸 문장의 역할을 먼저 판단하고, 근거 문장과 오답 배제 이유를 해설에서 확인하는 흐름입니다.

blocks.text: 풀이 순서: ① 빈칸 문장이 주제문인지, 재진술인지, 대조인지 판단 ② 근거 문장에 밑줄 ③ 선지를 근거와 하나씩 대응.

sections.en: Cartographers have long faced a quiet dilemma: a map that shows everything is a map nobody can read. A street plan that included every lamppost, bench, and mailbox would be so crowded that a traveler could not find the nearest station. Good mapmakers therefore decide what to leave out. They remove detail not because it is false, but because it would hide what the user needs. In this sense, the usefulness of a map comes from its careful omission. A reader who understands this will not complain that a hiking map omits the shops in the valley; she will ask instead what purpose the map was drawn to serve.

blocks.label: 빈칸 추론 · 쉬움
blocks.passage: Cartographers have long faced a quiet dilemma: a map that shows everything is a map nobody can read. A street plan that included every lamppost, bench, and mailbox would be so crowded that a traveler could not find the nearest station. Good mapmakers therefore decide what to leave out. They remove detail not because it is false, but because it would hide what the user needs. In this sense, the usefulness of a map comes from its ______. A reader who understands this will not complain that a hiking map omits the shops in the valley; she will ask instead what purpose the map was drawn to serve.
blocks.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 빈칸 문장은 앞 내용의 재진술입니다. 모든 것을 담은 지도는 읽을 수 없고, 좋은 제작자는 '무엇을 뺄지 결정한다'(leave out, remove detail)고 했으므로 지도의 유용성은 신중한 생략에서 나옵니다. 마지막 문장도 빠진 정보를 탓하지 말라는 내용으로 이를 뒷받침합니다.
wrong: ② complete coverage는 첫 두 문장에서 오히려 읽을 수 없는 지도의 원인으로 제시됨
③·④·⑤는 지도의 유용성과 관련된 근거가 지문에 없음

blocks.label: 빈칸 추론 · 표준
blocks.passage: When a team wins a game, fans often credit the final goal. Yet most of what decided the match happened earlier: a defender who closed a gap, a midfielder who chose a short pass instead of a risky one. These actions rarely appear in the highlights because they do not look dramatic. Their effect is nevertheless real, since each one ______. Understanding this changes how we judge any success, whether in sport or in work: the visible result is only the last link in a chain of quiet choices.
blocks.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: makes the next good action possible
attracts more attention than the goal
blocks.answer: ① makes the next good action possible
blocks.explain: 'chain of quiet choices'와 'last link'가 단서입니다. 눈에 띄지 않는 행동이 이후의 성공으로 이어지는 연결 고리라는 뜻이므로, 각 행동이 다음의 좋은 행동을 가능하게 한다는 ①이 맞습니다.
wrong: ④는 'do not look dramatic'과 정반대
③·⑤는 지문에 근거가 없음

blocks.text: 체크 포인트: 빈칸 앞에 In short, Therefore, in this sense 같은 표현이 있으면 앞 내용을 요약·재진술하는 빈칸입니다. 선지를 읽기 전에 빈칸에 들어갈 뜻을 우리말로 먼저 예상해 보세요.

blocks.label: 빈칸 추론 · 쉬움
blocks.passage: Many people believe that a good listener is simply someone who stays quiet. But silence alone does not help a speaker. A friend who stares at her phone while you talk is quiet, yet you feel ignored. Real listening shows itself in small responses: a nod at the right moment, a question that picks up a word you just used, a pause that gives you room to continue. In short, good listening is not the absence of speech but ______.
blocks.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: the habit of finishing others' sentences
the ability to remember every detail
blocks.answer: ③ visible attention to the speaker
blocks.explain: In short는 앞 내용을 정리합니다. 침묵만으로는 부족하고, 끄덕임·되묻기·기다림 같은 작은 반응으로 듣고 있음이 드러난다고 했으므로 '화자에게 보이는 주의'인 ③이 맞습니다.
wrong: ① 조언을 주는 재능은 지문에 나오지 않음
② 'a pause that gives you room to continue'와 반대로 말을 가로채는 행동
④·⑤는 근거 없음

blocks.label: 빈칸 추론 · 표준
blocks.passage: In a tide pool, animals face a harsh schedule. Twice a day the sea retreats, and the pool is exposed to sun, wind, and sudden changes in temperature and saltiness. Species that live there cannot simply move away. Instead, many have developed ways to tolerate the change: snails seal their shells, anemones pull in their tentacles, and crabs hide beneath wet seaweed. Their success therefore depends less on strength than on ______.
blocks.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: the ability to endure changing conditions
blocks.answer: ⑤ the ability to endure changing conditions
blocks.explain: 빈칸 앞의 therefore가 이끄는 결론입니다. 그곳의 동물은 이동할 수 없고 변화를 견디는 방법을 발달시켰다고 했으므로, 성공은 힘보다 '변하는 조건을 견디는 능력'에 달려 있습니다.
wrong: ① 'cannot simply move away'와 맞지 않음
②·③·④는 지문에 근거가 없음

blocks.label: 빈칸 추론 · 심화
blocks.passage: Scientists often present their findings in hedged language: 'the data suggest' or 'it is likely that'. Readers new to science sometimes take such phrases as signs of weakness, as if the researchers did not really know. In fact, the hedges tell the reader precisely how far the evidence reaches. A claim that sounds absolute, by contrast, usually hides how much remains unknown. Careful qualification is therefore a way of ______ rather than a lack of confidence.
blocks.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: being honest about the limits of the evidence
blocks.answer: ② being honest about the limits of the evidence
blocks.explain: 'the hedges tell the reader precisely how far the evidence reaches'가 핵심 단서입니다. 조심스러운 표현은 근거가 미치는 범위를 정직하게 알리는 방법이므로 ②입니다. rather than 뒤의 'lack of confidence'와 대비되는 긍정적 의미여야 합니다.
wrong: ① 책임 회피라는 해석은 지문의 평가와 반대
③·④·⑤는 지문에 근거가 없음

blocks.label: 빈칸 추론 · 표준
blocks.passage: In music, rests are not empty. A composer who writes a pause is deciding when the listener should wait, and that waiting makes the next note feel stronger. Players who rush through rests treat them as mistakes; skilled performers hold them as carefully as notes. A rest, in this sense, is part of the music because it ______.
blocks.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: gives the players time to leave
shows that the composer ran out of ideas
shapes how the following sound is heard
blocks.answer: ④ shapes how the following sound is heard
blocks.explain: 'that waiting makes the next note feel stronger'가 근거입니다. 쉼표는 이어지는 소리가 어떻게 들리는지를 좌우하므로 음악의 일부라는 ④가 맞습니다.
wrong: ② 작곡가의 의도적 결정이라고 했으므로 반대
③·⑤·① 은 지문에 근거가 없음

sections.en: Sleep researchers often compare the brain at night to a night-shift crew. While the body lies still, the brain is busy sorting the day's experiences. Important memories are strengthened, and trivial details are quietly discarded. Such selective editing is what makes the stored version of a day more useful than the original. A student who studies late and then sleeps normally often remembers more than one who studies all night. Without enough sleep, new information piles up like unsorted mail. Sleep, in other words, is part of learning, not a break from it.

blocks.label: 글의 순서 · 쉬움
blocks.passage:
Last spring, our school library started a seed exchange shelf.
(A) The next week, a student brought tomato seeds in a labeled envelope, and soon the shelf held herbs, beans, and flowers too.
(B) It began as a small experiment: a single box with a note asking readers to take what they needed and leave what they could spare.
(C) By summer, several classes were growing the borrowed plants on the roof, and the librarian had to ask for a bigger box.
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: (B)의 It은 주어진 글의 seed exchange shelf를 가리키며 a single box로 시작 상황을 소개합니다. (A)의 The next week는 그 시작 다음 주이고, (C)의 a bigger box는 (B)의 a single box와 대응하며 By summer로 가장 나중입니다.
wrong: (A)가 먼저 오면 The next week의 기준 시점이 없음
(C)가 먼저 오면 the borrowed plants가 소개된 적 없음

blocks.label: 문장 삽입 · 표준
blocks.passage:
Sleep researchers often compare the brain at night to a night-shift crew. ( ① ) While the body lies still, the brain is busy sorting the day's experiences. ( ② ) Important memories are strengthened, and trivial details are quietly discarded. ( ③ ) A student who studies late and then sleeps normally often remembers more than one who studies all night. ( ④ ) Without enough sleep, new information piles up like unsorted mail. ( ⑤ ) Sleep, in other words, is part of learning, not a break from it.

[주어진 문장] Such selective editing is what makes the stored version of a day more useful than the original.
blocks.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 주어진 문장의 Such selective editing은 '중요한 기억은 강화하고 사소한 것은 버린다'는 직전 내용을 가리킵니다. 따라서 그 문장 바로 뒤인 ③에 들어가야 하며, 이어지는 학생의 예는 편집된 기억이 더 유용하다는 말의 사례가 됩니다.
wrong: ② 앞에는 아직 editing에 해당하는 설명이 없어 Such가 받을 대상이 없음

blocks.text: 순서 풀이 팁: 후보를 두 개로 좁힌 뒤, 각 후보의 이음새(지시어·연결어·정관사)가 실제로 맞물리는지 문장 단위로 확인합니다. 삽입 풀이 팁: 주어진 문장에서 It, This, Such, However 같은 단서어를 먼저 밑줄 칩니다.

blocks.label: 글의 순서 · 표준
blocks.passage:
When the town of Linden decided to repaint its old footbridge, the council expected a quiet job.
(A) Before the first coat was even dry, however, residents began to stop by and share memories of crossing the bridge as children.
(B) Workers had planned to cover the faded blue with a modern gray that matched the new buildings nearby.
(C) In response, the council kept the original blue and added a small plaque telling those stories.
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: (B)는 repaint 계획의 내용(cover the faded blue)을 먼저 알려 줍니다. (A)의 the first coat는 칠이 시작된 뒤를 가리키고 however로 조용한 작업이라는 기대와 대비되며, (C)의 In response는 (A)의 주민 반응에 대한 대응이므로 마지막입니다.
wrong: (A)가 (B)보다 앞서면 the first coat가 가리킬 계획이 소개되지 않음
(C)가 (A)보다 앞서면 In response의 대상(주민 반응)이 없음

blocks.label: 글의 순서 · 심화
blocks.passage:
Researchers who study habits often separate external motivation from internal motivation.
(A) The former depends on rewards or pressure from outside, such as a prize for good grades or a parent's reminder.
(B) The latter, in contrast, comes from within, as when a person practices the piano simply because the music is enjoyable.
(C) Both can start a habit, but only the latter tends to keep it going once the rewards disappear.
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: the former/the latter는 먼저 소개된 두 대상을 순서대로 가리킵니다. 따라서 external(former)을 설명하는 (A)가 먼저, in contrast로 internal(latter)을 설명하는 (B)가 다음이며, Both로 둘을 함께 다루는 (C)가 마지막입니다.

Most people think of a museum as a place where objects sit still behind glass. ( ① ) Increasingly, however, curators are inviting visitors to touch, smell, and even handle some pieces. ( ② ) A textile museum, for example, lets visitors feel samples of wool and silk beside the framed originals. ( ③ ) Those who have tried this say they notice details that the eye alone misses, such as the weight of a cloth or the roughness of a thread. ( ④ ) Seeing, it turns out, is only one way of knowing an object. ( ⑤ )

[주어진 문장] They add that handling an object also makes it easier to remember later.

Many people think a coastline is a fixed line on a map. ( ① ) In reality, it moves with every tide, by a few meters in some places and by much more in others. ( ② ) Mapmakers therefore choose a rule, such as the average level of high tide, to decide where the land officially ends. ( ③ ) Different countries may choose different rules, so the same beach can be measured in different ways. ( ④ ) A coastline, then, is less a fact of nature than an agreement among people. ( ⑤ )

[주어진 문장] This means that two surveyors measuring at different hours may honestly report different lengths for the same shore.

sections.en: Many towns now have 'libraries of things' where residents can borrow items other than books: ladders, sewing machines, camping stoves, even karaoke sets. The idea is simple. Most household tools are used only a few hours a year, yet each family buys its own and stores it in a closet. By sharing, a neighborhood can reduce spending and clutter at the same time. Supporters add that the arrangement has a social benefit. A person who comes to borrow a drill often stays to chat with a volunteer or a neighbor, and these small conversations help strangers become familiar faces. Critics worry that popular items may be unavailable when needed, but organizers answer that a reservation system solves most of these problems.

sections.en: Every autumn, Mina's grandfather raked the fallen leaves into one big pile at the edge of the yard. He did not burn them or send them away; he simply let them sit through the cold months. Snow covered the pile, and the leaves slowly softened underneath. blocks.label: 글의 순서 · 쉬움
blocks.passage:
Ms. Han ran a small bakery, and for years she sold only plain bread.
(A) Customers began asking for it, and within a month the sesame loaf outsold every other item on the shelf.
(B) One morning, she ran out of flour for her usual recipe and mixed in some toasted sesame seeds she had been saving.
(C) Surprised by how good the loaf smelled, she put a few on the counter with a handwritten sign: 'Today's experiment.'
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: (B)의 One morning이 사건의 시작이고 참깨를 섞은 빵이 처음 나옵니다. (C)의 the loaf는 (B)에서 만든 빵을 정관사로 받고, (A)의 it은 (C)에서 진열된 빵을 가리키며 결과를 말합니다.
wrong: (C)가 (B)보다 앞서면 the loaf가 소개되지 않음
(A)가 (C)보다 앞서면 'Today's experiment' 진열 이후의 결과가 먼저 나오는 모순

blocks.label: 글의 순서 · 표준
blocks.passage:
Scientists who study bird migration face a practical problem: birds travel at night, when they are almost impossible to watch.
(A) Researchers therefore turned to radar, which can detect flocks moving through the dark even when no one can see them.
(B) The combined data surprised them: on some nights, millions of birds, representing dozens of species, crossed a single region.
(C) Radar images, however, show only moving shapes, so the team also recorded the birds' calls to identify the species.
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: (A)는 therefore로 주어진 글의 문제에 대한 해결책(radar)을 제시합니다. (C)의 Radar images는 (A)를 받고 however로 한계를 말하며 울음소리 기록을 추가합니다. (B)의 The combined data는 레이더와 울음소리 데이터를 합친 것이므로 마지막입니다.
wrong: (B)가 (C)보다 앞서면 species 식별과 combined data의 근거가 없음

blocks.text: 체크 포인트: 처음 보는 명사에는 a/an, 이미 나온 명사에는 the를 씁니다. the + 명사가 먼저 나오면 그 앞에 소개 문장이 있어야 합니다.

blocks.label: 글의 순서 · 쉬움
blocks.passage:
Every autumn, Mina's grandfather raked the fallen leaves into one big pile at the edge of the yard.
(A) By spring, the pile had turned into dark, crumbly soil that smelled like the forest floor.
(B) Then he spread the soil around the vegetable beds, and the tomatoes grew taller than ever.
(C) He did not burn them or send them away; he simply let them sit through the cold months. Snow covered the pile, and the leaves slowly softened underneath.
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: (C)의 them은 주어진 글의 leaves를 받고, 태우지 않고 겨울 동안 둔다는 과정의 시작을 말합니다. (A)의 By spring은 cold months 다음 시점이며, (B)의 Then은 흙이 된 뒤에 뿌리는 마지막 단계입니다.
wrong: (A)가 (C)보다 앞서면 By spring의 기준이 되는 겨울이 먼저 나오지 않음
(B)가 앞서면 the soil이 소개되기 전에 쓰임

blocks.label: 글의 순서 · 표준
blocks.passage:
A café near our school once noticed that its trash bins were filling up with paper cups faster than with any other kind of waste.
(A) At first, few people took the offer, because carrying a cup around seemed like a hassle.
(B) So the owner decided to give a small discount to anyone who brought a reusable cup.
(C) Within a few months, however, the habit spread, and the bins held far fewer paper cups.
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: (B)의 So는 주어진 글의 문제(종이컵 쓰레기)에 대한 해결책이고, (A)의 the offer는 (B)의 할인 제안을 받습니다. (C)의 however는 (A)의 At first(처음에는 적었다)와 대비되는 결과이므로 마지막입니다.
wrong: (A)가 (B)보다 앞서면 the offer가 소개되지 않음
(C)가 (A)보다 앞서면 however가 대비할 At first의 상황이 없음

blocks.label: 글의 순서 · 표준
blocks.passage:
Many people assume that creativity strikes suddenly, like a flash of light.
(A) That hidden work is easy to overlook, which is why the final idea seems to appear from nowhere.
(B) In fact, the notebooks of many writers and designers are full of rough attempts that came long before any 'sudden' idea.
(C) Each of those attempts removes a weak option, and the pile of discarded drafts is what makes the final idea possible.
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: (B)의 In fact는 주어진 글의 통념과 반대되는 사실(노트의 초안들)을 제시합니다. (C)의 those attempts는 (B)의 rough attempts를 받고, (A)의 That hidden work는 (B)·(C)에서 설명한 보이지 않는 작업을 가리켜 결론을 맺습니다.
wrong: (A)가 앞서면 That hidden work가 가리킬 작업이 아직 소개되지 않음
(C)가 (B)보다 앞서면 those attempts의 대상이 없음

blocks.label: 글의 순서 · 심화
blocks.passage:
For generations, the villagers of Ora had gathered every morning at the single well in the square.

(C) The well was no longer needed, and some feared the square would fall silent.
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: (B)의 That habit은 주어진 글의 '매일 아침 우물에 모이는 습관'을 가리키며 변화의 계기를 말합니다. (C)는 우물이 필요 없어져 광장이 조용해질 것이라는 우려이고, (A)의 Yet은 그 우려와 대비되어 광장이 계속 붐볐다는 결과를 말하므로 마지막입니다.
wrong: (A)가 (C)보다 앞서면 대비할 우려가 먼저 나오지 않아 Yet이 어색함

sections.en: Cities are often noisier than people realize. Traffic, construction, and sirens blend into a constant background that residents learn to ignore. Yet the body does not fully ignore it. In other words, getting used to noise is not the same as being unaffected by it. Sleep experiments suggest that sudden sounds can raise the heart rate even when the sleeper does not wake. Planners are therefore paying more attention to quiet spaces such as courtyards and tree-lined streets.

blocks.label: 문장 삽입 · 표준
blocks.passage:
Many people picture inventors as lone geniuses working in silence. ( ① ) The history of everyday objects tells a different story. ( ② ) Most useful devices were improved step by step by many hands, each person fixing a flaw the last had left. ( ③ ) The bicycle, for instance, went through several odd forms before the familiar chain-driven design appeared. ( ④ ) Invention, then, is usually a shared and gradual effort. ( ⑤ )

[주어진 문장] Many of them never met one another, yet each learned from the mistakes of those before.
blocks.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 주어진 문장의 Many of them은 자전거의 여러 이상한 형태를 만든 설계자들을 가리킵니다. 자전거 예시 바로 뒤인 ④에 놓으면 다음 문장의 결론 Invention, then, ...으로 자연스럽게 이어집니다.
wrong: ③ 앞에는 them이 가리킬 복수 대상이 'many hands'뿐이고, 뒤에 for instance 예시가 와서 흐름이 어색함
⑤는 결론 뒤라서 them이 받을 대상이 부적절함

blocks.label: 문장 삽입 · 표준

Cities are often noisier than people realize. ( ① ) Traffic, construction, and sirens blend into a constant background that residents learn to ignore. ( ② ) Yet the body does not fully ignore it. ( ③ ) Sleep experiments suggest that sudden sounds can raise the heart rate even when the sleeper does not wake. ( ④ ) Planners are therefore paying more attention to quiet spaces such as courtyards and tree-lined streets. ( ⑤ )

[주어진 문장] In other words, getting used to noise is not the same as being unaffected by it.
blocks.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: In other words는 직전 문장을 풀어 말할 때 쓰입니다. 'the body does not fully ignore it'을 '익숙해지는 것과 영향을 받지 않는 것은 다르다'로 바꿔 말한 것이므로 ③이 맞고, 뒤의 수면 실험이 그 근거가 됩니다.

blocks.label: 문장 삽입 · 쉬움
blocks.passage:
Learning to cook is often described as learning to follow recipes. ( ① ) But experienced cooks say the real skill is tasting as you go. ( ② ) A beginner may follow every step exactly yet never taste the food. ( ③ ) By contrast, a cook who tastes at each stage keeps checking the dish against what she wants. ( ④ ) Recipes, then, are best seen as a starting point rather than a rule book. ( ⑤ )

[주어진 문장] As a result, the dish may turn out too salty or too bland, and nobody notices until it is served.
blocks.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: As a result는 원인에 이어지는 결과를 말합니다. '초보자는 따라 하기만 하고 맛을 보지 않는다'가 원인이므로 그 바로 뒤인 ③에 들어가고, 다음 문장 By contrast가 맛을 보는 요리사와 대비합니다.
wrong: ② 앞은 맛보기가 핵심이라는 내용이어서 '짜거나 싱거운 결과'의 원인이 아님
④ 뒤에서는 맛을 보는 요리사의 이야기라서 결과가 맞지 않음

blocks.text: 체크 포인트: 같은 지시어가 여러 곳에 맞는 것처럼 보이면, 뒤 문장이 주어진 문장 없이도 자연스러운지 확인합니다. 정답 위치에서는 뒤 문장이 주어진 문장을 이어받습니다.

blocks.passage:
Roads shape the lives of wild animals as well as those of people. ( ① ) For many species, a highway is a barrier: small animals avoid open pavement, and larger ones risk being hit by cars. ( ② ) Some countries have therefore built wide, planted bridges over their highways for animals to use. ( ③ ) Cameras there have recorded deer, foxes, and many smaller animals crossing. ( ④ ) Such structures are expensive, but they show that a road need not be a wall. ( ⑤ )

[주어진 문장] Over time, groups living on opposite sides of it may stop meeting and become isolated from one another.
blocks.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 주어진 문장의 it은 '장벽'이 된 highway를 가리키며, Over time ... isolated는 동물이 도로를 피하거나 치일 위험이 있다는 직전 내용의 결과입니다. ②에 넣으면 다음 문장의 therefore(그래서 다리를 만들었다)가 이 문제에 대한 대응이 되어 자연스럽습니다.

blocks.label: 문장 삽입 · 심화
blocks.passage:
Languages borrow words constantly, and English is no exception. ( ① ) Words like 'piano' and 'karaoke' arrived together with the things they name. ( ② ) In these cases, the borrowed word filled a gap, since English had no ready term. ( ③ ) Yet words are sometimes borrowed even when a native term already exists. ( ④ ) Speakers may feel that the foreign word carries a tone or prestige that the older word lacks. ( ⑤ )

[주어진 문장] In short, borrowing answers to image as much as to need.
blocks.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: In short는 앞 내용을 요약합니다. 필요 때문에 빌린 경우(②~③)와 이미 말이 있어도 이미지 때문에 빌리는 경우(④~⑤)를 모두 다룬 뒤이므로 마지막 ⑤가 맞습니다. ④에 넣으면 이어지는 문장이 요약 뒤에 세부 설명으로 남아 흐름이 어색합니다.
wrong: ④ 뒤의 문장이 이미지 쪽 설명을 완성하므로 요약은 그 뒤에 와야 함
③ 앞에는 need 쪽만 나와 as much as to need의 대비가 성립하지 않음

blocks.passage:
Many students treat a mistake on a test as a verdict on their ability. ( ① ) A better habit is to treat it as information. ( ② ) A wrong answer shows exactly which idea has not yet been understood. ( ③ ) Students who review their errors in this way often improve faster than those who only check their scores. ( ④ ) The score tells you where you are, but the errors show you where to go next. ( ⑤ )

sections.en: Many students think that memory improves by simply reading a text again and again. However, testing yourself is far more effective, because it forces the brain to retrieve information rather than just recognize it. A student who practices recalling the main points without looking at the notes finds it easier to remember them later. This is why many teachers now encourage short quizzes in class. Short quizzes of this kind also take less time than rereading a whole chapter.

blocks.label: 어법성 판단 · 표준
blocks.passage: Many students think that memory [① improves] by simply reading a text again and again. However, testing yourself is far more effective, because it forces the brain [② to retrieve] information rather than just recognize it. A student [③ who] practices recalling the main points without looking at the notes [④ find] it easier to remember them later. This is why many teachers now [⑤ encourage] short quizzes in class. Short quizzes of this kind also take less time than rereading a whole chapter.
blocks.question: 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
blocks.explain: 주어는 단수인 A student이고 who ... notes는 이를 꾸미는 관계절입니다. 따라서 동사는 단수형 finds여야 합니다.
wrong: ② force + 목적어 + to부정사 구문이 맞음
⑤ many teachers가 복수 주어라 encourage가 맞음

blocks.label: 어법 선택 · 표준
blocks.passage: The report suggests that the number of people (A)[who / which] cycle to work has doubled. City officials, (B)[pleasing / pleased] by the change, plan to build more bike lanes. They hope that traffic jams, (C)[that / which] have troubled the downtown area for years, will become less frequent.
blocks.question: (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks.explain: (A) 선행사가 사람(people)이므로 who. (B) 관리들이 기뻐함을 당하는 감정이므로 과거분사 pleased. (C) 쉼표 뒤의 계속적 용법에는 that을 쓸 수 없고 which를 씁니다.
wrong: ① (A) which는 선행사가 사람(people)이라 who가 맞음
② (B) pleasing은 능동·현재분사라서 '기쁘게 하는'의 뜻이 되어 관리들이 기뻐함과 맞지 않음
③ (C) 쉼표 뒤 계속적 용법에는 that을 쓸 수 없음
⑤ (A)·(C) 모두 위 이유로 부적절함

blocks.label: 어법성 판단 · 쉬움
blocks.passage: Volunteers at the animal shelter [① are] asked to arrive by eight o'clock. Each morning, they clean the cages and [② feeding] the dogs before the visitors come. A young volunteer, [③ named] Hana, says that the work taught her [④ to be] patient with animals. After a few months, she found [⑤ it] easy to calm even the shyest puppies.
blocks.question: 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

wrong: ① Volunteers가 주어이므로 are asked(수동태)가 맞음
③ 'who is named'에서 줄어든 과거분사 named가 Hana를 꾸밈
④ teach + 목적어 + to부정사 구문
⑤ find + it(가목적어) + 형용사 + to부정사 구문

blocks.label: 어법성 판단 · 표준
blocks.passage: The city library, [① which] opened two years ago, has a rooftop garden [② where] visitors can read among the plants. The garden, [③ designing] by a local architect, collects rainwater and uses it to water the flowers. Visitors say that sitting there makes them [④ feel] calm, and many of them add that [⑤ what] they enjoy most is the quiet.

blocks.label: 어법 선택 · 표준
blocks.passage: Running a marathon requires months of preparation, and runners who train (A)[carefully / careful] often finish with fewer injuries. Many beginners are surprised (B)[that / what] the hardest part is not the distance but the discipline of daily practice. By the time race day arrives, those who have followed a plan feel as if the course (C)[were / have been] an old friend.

blocks.explain: (A) 동사 train을 꾸미므로 부사 carefully. (B) 뒤에 완전한 절이 오므로 접속사 that(what은 불완전한 절 뒤). (C) as if 가정법에서는 were를 씁니다.

②·④ (B) what 뒤에는 불완전한 절이 와야 함

sections.en: Wetlands are often seen as useless land, but they are in fact highly beneficial. They absorb heavy rain like a sponge, which reduces flooding downstream. They also provide homes for birds and fish and help sustain local fishing. When wetlands are drained for roads and farms, these benefits diminish quickly. Protecting them is therefore a sensible investment.

blocks.passage: A good traveler knows that rules about politeness differ widely. In some countries, looking directly at an elder is a sign of (A)[respect / disrespect], while in others it is considered rude. A visitor who ignores such differences may cause (B)[offense / pleasure] without intending to. blocks.question: (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

wrong: ① (A) disrespect는 뒤의 'considered rude'와 대조되지 않음
③ (B) pleasure는 차이를 무시한 결과로 어색함
④ (C) ignore는 관찰한 뒤 행동을 맞춘다는 흐름과 반대
⑤ (A)·(B)·(C) 모두 문맥과 어긋남

blocks.label: 어휘 의미 · 쉬움
blocks.passage: Although the manager was reluctant to approve the plan, she finally agreed after seeing the revised budget.
blocks.question: 밑줄 친 reluctant의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?
blocks.explain: Although가 이끄는 양보절이므로 '결국 동의했다'와 대조되는 뜻이 필요합니다. reluctant는 '꺼리는'이므로 unwilling과 가깝습니다.
wrong: ② eager는 reluctant와 반대 의미
③·④·⑤는 양보절과 '결국 동의했다'의 대조에서 나오는 뜻이 아님

blocks.label: 어휘 의미 · 표준
blocks.passage: Her reply was ambiguous, so the committee could not tell whether she supported the plan.
blocks.question: 밑줄 친 ambiguous의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?
blocks.explain: so 이하에서 위원회가 그녀가 계획을 지지하는지 알 수 없었다고 했으므로 답이 분명하지 않았다는 뜻입니다. ambiguous는 unclear와 가깝습니다.
wrong: ① honest는 지지 여부를 알 수 없었다는 결과와 이어지지 않음
② 짧은 답이라는 근거가 없음
④·⑤도 근거가 없음

blocks.text: 체크 포인트: 같은 단어라도 품사와 쓰임이 문장마다 다릅니다. 빈칸 뒤에 목적어가 있는지(타동사), 앞뒤가 대조인지 같은 방향인지를 먼저 보세요.

blocks.label: 문맥 속 어휘 · 표준
blocks.passage: Many people think that a small mistake is (A)[trivial / serious] and not worth fixing. But an unchecked error in a calendar or a bill can (B)[hinder / assist] your plans for weeks. It is therefore wise to (C)[neglect / review] your records once a week.
blocks.question: (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks.explain: (A) '고칠 가치가 없다'고 여기는 것은 trivial한 실수입니다. (B) But 뒤에서 확인하지 않은 오류가 계획에 나쁜 영향을 주므로 hinder. (C) therefore 이하는 기록을 점검하라는 권유이므로 review입니다.
wrong: ① (A) serious이면 '고칠 가치가 없다'와 맞지 않음
② (B) assist는 But 앞뒤의 대조와 맞지 않음
③ (C) neglect는 therefore 뒤 권유와 반대
⑤ (A)·(B)·(C) 모두 반대

blocks.label: 어휘 의미 · 심화
blocks.passage: A river does not suddenly dry up; it ______ little by little as the dry months pass, until only a thin stream remains.
blocks.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks.explain: little by little ... until only a thin stream remains는 서서히 줄어든다는 뜻이고, 빈칸 뒤에 목적어가 없으므로 자동사로 쓰인 diminishes가 맞습니다.
wrong: ① conceals·③ consumes·④ hinders는 목적어가 필요한 타동사이며 의미도 맞지 않음
⑤ sustains는 '유지하다'라서 줄어드는 흐름과 반대

blocks.label: 어휘 문맥 · 심화
blocks.passage: Wetlands are often seen as useless land, but they are in fact highly [① beneficial]. They absorb heavy rain like a sponge, which [② reduces] flooding downstream. They also provide homes for birds and fish and help [③ sustain] local fishing. When wetlands are drained for roads and farms, these benefits [④ increase] quickly. Protecting them is therefore a sensible [⑤ investment].
blocks.question: 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
blocks.explain: 습지를 매립하면 앞에서 말한 이점이 사라지므로 increase가 아니라 diminish처럼 줄어든다는 뜻의 낱말이 필요합니다. 마지막 문장의 therefore(보호하자)도 이점이 줄어든다는 내용과 이어집니다.
wrong: ① 앞의 'useless'와 but으로 대조되는 긍정적 낱말
② 빗물을 흡수해 홍수를 줄인다는 문맥에 맞음
③ 어업을 유지하도록 돕는다는 문맥에 맞음
⑤ 보호를 투자에 비유한 문맥에 맞음

blocks.label: 요지 · 표준
blocks.question: 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. (윗글 참고)
choices: Draining wetlands is the best way to prevent floods.
Wetlands bring benefits that are worth protecting.
Fishing should be banned near wetlands.
Roads and farms are more valuable than wetlands.
Birds and fish are the only reason to keep wetlands.
blocks.answer: ② Wetlands bring benefits that are worth protecting.
blocks.explain: 습지가 홍수를 줄이고 생물의 서식지가 되며 어업을 유지하는 이점이 있고, 마지막 문장에서 보호가 현명한 투자라고 했으므로 ②가 요지입니다.
wrong: ① 습지는 오히려 홍수를 줄이는 역할을 함
④ 도로와 농지가 더 가치 있다는 근거가 없음
⑤ 새와 물고기만이 이유라는 것은 과한 일반화

blocks.question: 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

sentences.en: Wetlands are often seen as useless land, {{but|연결사}} they are in fact highly {{beneficial|어휘}}.
sentences.ko: 습지는 흔히 쓸모없는 땅으로 여겨지지만, 사실은 매우 유익하다.

sentences.en: They absorb heavy rain like a sponge, {{which|문법}} {{reduces|어휘}} flooding downstream.
sentences.ko: 습지는 스펀지처럼 폭우를 흡수하며, 그것이 하류의 홍수를 줄여 준다.

sentences.en: They also provide homes for birds and fish and help {{sustain|어휘}} local fishing.
sentences.ko: 습지는 또한 새와 물고기에게 서식지를 제공하고 지역 어업을 유지하는 데 도움을 준다.

sentences.en: When wetlands are drained for roads and farms, these benefits {{diminish|어휘}} quickly.
sentences.ko: 습지의 물을 빼서 도로와 농지로 만들면 이런 이점은 빠르게 줄어든다.

sentences.en: Protecting them is {{therefore|연결사}} a sensible {{investment|어휘}}.
sentences.ko: 그러므로 습지를 보호하는 것은 현명한 투자이다.

blocks.note: ④의 원문 표현 increase는 앞뒤 문맥(이점이 사라짐, therefore 보호)과 어긋나는 낱말이어서, 여기서는 문맥에 맞게 diminish(줄어들다)로 바로잡아 표시했습니다.

sections.en: Good afternoon, students. This is Ms. Lee from the school library. As you know, the library will be closed for floor repairs from next Monday to Wednesday. During this time, you will not be able to borrow or return books at the desk. However, a return box will be placed in front of the main entrance, and books returned there will be counted as on time. The reading room on the second floor will stay open as usual. If you have any questions, please visit the library website. Thank you.

blocks.label: 대화 듣기 · 표준
blocks.passage:
M: Hi, Jiwoo. Did you finish the poster for the science fair?
W: Yes, it's ready. I only need to print it, but the printer room closes at five today.
M: Then you'd better hurry. By the way, did you book a table for our group?
W: I did it yesterday online. Table number twelve, near the entrance.
M: Great. Oh, and Mr. Park said everyone must bring their own tape to fix the poster.
W: Right, I have some at home. I'll also bring a spare roll for you.
M: Thanks! Then I'll bring the extra batteries for the projector.
W: Perfect. I'll go to the printer room now.
blocks.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 대화 직후에 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 여자는 포스터를 인쇄만 하면 되는데 인쇄실이 5시에 닫는다고 했고, 마지막에 'I'll go to the printer room now'라고 말합니다. 테이블은 이미 예약했고 테이프는 집에 있습니다.
wrong: ① 이미 어제 예약함
④ 건전지는 남자가 가져옴

blocks.label: 담화 듣기 · 표준
blocks.passage: W: Good afternoon, students. This is Ms. Lee from the school library. As you know, the library will be closed for floor repairs from next Monday to Wednesday. During this time, you will not be able to borrow or return books at the desk. However, a return box will be placed in front of the main entrance, and books returned there will be counted as on time. The reading room on the second floor will stay open as usual. If you have any questions, please visit the library website. Thank you.
blocks.question: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: to announce a library closing and how to return books
to ask students to donate used books
to introduce a new reading program
to explain how to renew a library card
blocks.answer: ① to announce a library closing and how to return books
blocks.explain: 공사로 인한 휴관 기간을 알리고, 그동안 반납함으로 기한 내 반납이 인정된다는 방법을 안내하므로 ①입니다.
wrong: ② 기부 요청은 언급되지 않음
③ 새 독서 프로그램은 언급되지 않음
④ 도서관 이용증 갱신은 언급되지 않음
⑤ 봉사자 모집은 언급되지 않음

blocks.label: 대화 듣기 · 쉬움
blocks.passage:
W: Dad, can you drive me to the swimming pool tomorrow?
M: Sorry, I have to take the car to the repair shop in the morning.
W: Oh. My lesson starts at ten.
M: How about taking the bus? Bus number 7 stops right in front of the pool.
W: That's a good idea. But my bag is heavy because of the towels and goggles.
M: Then I'll walk you to the bus stop and carry the bag.
W: Thanks, Dad. I'll leave the house at nine thirty.
blocks.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 내일 수영장에 가는 방법으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 아버지가 차를 수리점에 맡겨야 해서 태워 줄 수 없고, 7번 버스가 수영장 앞에 선다고 제안하자 여자가 좋은 생각이라고 답했습니다. 정류장까지 걸어가기는 하지만 수영장까지의 방법은 버스입니다.
wrong: ① 차는 수리점에 가야 함
④ 정류장까지만 걷는 것
③·⑤는 언급되지 않음

blocks.text: 체크 포인트: 대화에서 먼저 나온 말이 곧 정답이 아닙니다. 중간에 나온 선택지는 뒤에서 취소되거나 이미 끝난 일인 경우가 많으므로, 마지막에 확정된 내용을 확인하세요.

blocks.label: 대화 듣기 · 표준
blocks.passage:
W: Minho, are you coming to the book club on Friday?
M: I wanted to, but I can't this time.
W: Is it because of the exam?
M: Not really. I've finished studying. I have to go to my cousin's graduation ceremony that evening.
W: Oh, that sounds nice. Is it far?
M: It's in Busan, so I'll take the train after school.
W: I see. We'll send you the book notes so you can catch up.
M: Thanks, that would help.
blocks.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 독서 모임에 참석할 수 없는 이유로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: to take care of his cousin
blocks.answer: ④ to attend a graduation ceremony
blocks.explain: 여자가 시험 때문이냐고 묻자 남자는 Not really라고 부정하고 사촌의 졸업식에 가야 한다고 밝힙니다.
wrong: ① 시험 공부는 이미 끝냈다고 함
⑤ 사촌을 돌보는 것이 아니라 졸업식 참석
②·③은 언급되지 않음

blocks.label: 대화 듣기 · 표준
blocks.passage:
M: Welcome to Green Fields Farm Shop. May I help you?
W: Yes, I'd like two jars of strawberry jam and one bag of walnuts, please.
M: Sure. The jam is six dollars a jar, and a bag of walnuts is eight dollars.
W: Is there any discount?
M: If you buy three or more items, we take two dollars off the total.
W: Great. Then I'll take those. Oh, and I'd like to pay by card.
M: No problem.
blocks.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 잼 2병은 6달러 × 2 = 12달러, 호두 1봉지는 8달러이므로 합계 20달러입니다. 세 개를 샀으므로 2달러가 할인되어 18달러를 지불합니다.
wrong: ④ $20은 할인 전 금액
①·②·⑤는 계산과 맞지 않음

blocks.question: 다음을 듣고, 안내된 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.

blocks.answer: ⑤ The campaign will end in the evening.
blocks.explain: 행사는 정오(noon)에 끝난다고 했으므로 저녁에 끝난다는 ⑤가 일치하지 않습니다.
wrong: ①은 모이는 장소가 교문

sections.en: In many parks, you can find narrow dirt trails cutting across the grass where no path was ever planned. Landscape designers call them desire paths, because they show where people actually want to walk. A paved route might curve politely around a lawn, but pedestrians in a hurry will choose the shortest line to the gate, and after a few weeks of footsteps, the grass gives way to bare earth. Some planners once treated these trails as a problem and put up fences. Others have learned to treat them as free information. By watching where the ground wears away, they can see what no survey has captured: the routes that people find natural. A few universities now wait a season before laying their walkways, then pave over the paths students have already drawn with their feet. The result is a network that looks less tidy on a plan, but that fits daily life far better.

blocks.passage: Most of us treat boredom as an enemy. The moment a line grows long or a bus is late, a hand reaches for the phone. Yet some psychologists argue that an empty moment is not wasted. When nothing demands our attention, the mind begins to wander, linking memories, worries, and half-formed plans in ways that focused work does not allow. Many people report that their best ideas arrive in just such moments: in the shower, on a walk, while washing dishes. This does not mean that we should seek boredom for its own sake, and constant idleness brings its own problems. But a day packed from morning to night leaves no room for the mind's quiet work. Perhaps the wiser habit is to leave a few small gaps in the schedule and to resist the urge to fill every one of them.

blocks.passage: Before the railways, each town set its clocks by the sun, so noon in one city came a few minutes before noon in the next. This caused little trouble while travel was slow. Once trains began to run on timetables, however, the small differences became a real problem: a schedule that listed one departure time could mean different moments in different stations. Railway companies therefore adopted a single time for all their stations, and over the following decades many countries agreed on shared time zones. Not everyone welcomed the change. Some towns felt that giving up the sun's time meant giving up part of their independence. Yet the benefit was hard to deny, because a shared clock let strangers in distant places plan the same hour. In this way, a technology built for travel ended up changing the way ordinary people lived with time.

sections.en: Economists sometimes say that a price is a message. When a harvest fails and the price of grain rises, the increase is not only a cost; it is a signal telling every buyer, in a single number, that grain has become scarcer. No one has to explain the shortage, and no central office has to coordinate the response. Bakers use less, some farmers plant more, and distant traders look for new supplies. Because the message is so compact, however, it carries no explanation of why the grain is scarce, and a buyer who forgets this may blame the seller. A price, in other words, coordinates behavior efficiently but hides the reasons behind it.

A word-for-word version may keep the surface of the text and still lose its tone, while a freer version may keep the tone and lose some precision. Because no single solution preserves everything, translation is better described as ______ than as simple copying.
blocks.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: a mechanical exchange of equal words
an effort to remove the author's voice
a task that requires no judgment
a series of trade-offs made on the reader's behalf
a method of shortening long texts

The idea that a larger choice always makes people happier has been questioned in recent years.
(A) Faced with dozens of nearly identical options, shoppers can end up feeling less satisfied with whatever they pick, since each rejected option becomes a possible regret.
(B) This does not mean that options are harmful in themselves; it means their value depends on how easily a person can compare them.
(C) One reason for their dissatisfaction is that the effort of comparing so many details itself becomes a cost.
blocks.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

blocks.label: 고난도 문장 삽입 · 심화
blocks.passage:
When a damaged painting is restored, the restorer faces a question that has no purely technical answer. ( ① ) Should missing paint be filled in so that the picture looks whole, or should the gaps be left visible as honest traces of age? ( ② ) Those who favor full repair argue that a complete image lets viewers appreciate the artist's design. ( ③ ) Opponents reply that invented details may mislead future viewers about what the artist actually painted. ( ④ ) Many museums now choose a middle path, repairing the surface in a way that can be reversed and clearly recorded. ( ⑤ )

[주어진 문장] Behind the disagreement lies a deeper choice between the pleasure of a finished image and the duty to be truthful about the past.
blocks.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 주어진 문장의 the disagreement는 완전 복원을 지지하는 쪽과 반대하는 쪽의 의견 충돌을 가리킵니다. 두 입장이 모두 나온 뒤인 ④에 들어가며, 이어지는 문장(절충안)이 그 선택에 대한 해법이 됩니다.

blocks.label: 요약문 완성 · 심화
blocks.passage:
In many open-plan offices, workers wear headphones to shut out the chatter of colleagues. The immediate effect is a quieter mind and a gain in focus. Over time, however, people who isolate themselves this way may also lose the small, unplanned conversations that spread information and ideas across a team. A question asked in passing at the coffee machine, or a problem overheard and solved by a neighbor, rarely happens when everyone is wearing headphones. Companies that notice this problem sometimes set aside quiet rooms for focused work so that the open floor can stay open for talk.

[요약문] Using headphones in open offices can improve individual (A) ______ but may reduce (B) ______ among colleagues.
blocks.question: 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks.explain: 헤드폰은 개인의 집중(focus)을 높이지만, 지나가며 묻고 듣는 비공식 대화가 사라져 동료 간 교류(interaction)가 줄 수 있다는 것이 글의 흐름입니다.

Dear Mr. Collins,
I am writing on behalf of the Greenfield Neighborhood Association. Our community garden has grown quickly, and we now have more members than plots. The empty lot behind your hardware store has been unused for several years, and we wonder whether you would allow us to use a part of it for additional vegetable beds. We would be responsible for cleaning the site, and we would remove everything if you needed the space back. I would be glad to show you our plan in person at your convenience.
Sincerely,
Dana Weller

blocks.title: 어휘 표 예시 (14개)
rows: Wild berries are abundant in the northern forest.
Each member contributed an idea to the project.
Do not hesitate to ask if you need help.
The survey revealed a change in reading habits.
It takes effort to maintain a healthy routine.
Clear goals are essential for steady progress.
The map was accurate enough to guide us through the old town.
Pack the fragile cups in a thick layer of paper.
It took her a week to recover from the cold.
A temporary bridge was built while the old one was repaired.
You can obtain a library card with a student ID.
Compare the two maps and tell me what has changed.
The hikers found shelter under a rock during the storm.
There has been a gradual rise in the number of cyclists.
blocks.note: 예문은 쓰임을 보이기 위해 새로 쓴 문장입니다. 뜻은 문장 속 용법 위주로 정리합니다.

blocks.text: 학습 요령: 단어의 뜻만 외우지 말고 예문을 소리 내어 읽으며 어떤 단어와 함께 쓰이는지(recover from, contribute to)를 같이 확인합니다.

sections.en: After the storm, the town set up a temporary shelter in the school gym. The gym was warm and dry, and it had room for many beds. Volunteers brought blankets, and neighbors shared food, so supplies were abundant by evening. Doctors from the clinic stopped by to check on the elderly guests. The mayor said the shelter would close once repairs were finished, and she asked residents to be patient because the recovery would be gradual.

sections.en: A Shelter Until Repairs Are Done

sections.en: A school gym served as a well-supplied shelter, which will close when repairs are finished.

summary.structure: 논리 구조: 상황(폭풍 후 임시 대피소) → 시설(체육관) → 지원(자원봉사·이웃·의사) → 안내(시장: 수리 후 폐쇄, 인내 요청)
summary.theme: 임시 대피소의 상황과 향후 계획을 안내하는 글이다.

blocks.label: 어휘 빈칸 · 표준
blocks.passage: The detective was careful not to ______ any details of the case to reporters.
blocks.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks.explain: 빈칸 뒤에 목적어 any details가 오므로 타동사가 필요하고, '기자들에게 밝히지 않으려고 조심했다'는 의미에 맞는 것은 reveal입니다.
wrong: ③ hesitate와 ⑤ wander는 자동사로 목적어를 바로 취하지 못함
④ contribute는 to가 필요함

blocks.label: 어휘 의미 · 쉬움
blocks.passage: Fruit is abundant in this region, so prices stay low.
blocks.question: 밑줄 친 abundant와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
blocks.explain: 'so prices stay low'에서 공급이 많다는 뜻을 알 수 있으므로 abundant는 plentiful과 같은 의미입니다.
wrong: ① rare는 abundant와 반대 의미
③·④·⑤는 가격이 낮다는 근거와 연결되지 않음

blocks.label: 어휘 빈칸 · 쉬움
blocks.passage: Please handle the glass vase with care; it is very ______.
blocks.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks.explain: 유리 꽃병을 조심해서 다루라는 이유가 되는 말이므로 '깨지기 쉬운'이라는 뜻의 fragile이 맞습니다.
wrong: ① temporary는 '일시적인'이라 조심하라는 이유로 부적절
②·④·⑤도 문맥과 맞지 않음

blocks.label: 어휘 빈칸 · 표준
blocks.passage: It took her several weeks to ______ from the flu, but she finally returned to school.
blocks.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks.explain: '독감에서 ~하는 데 몇 주가 걸렸고 마침내 학교로 돌아왔다'는 문맥이므로 recover from(~에서 회복하다)이 맞습니다.
wrong: ① obtain은 '얻다'라서 from the flu와 의미가 맞지 않음
② compare·③ hesitate·⑤ maintain도 문맥과 맞지 않음

blocks.label: 어휘 의미 · 표준
blocks.passage: After the storm, the town set up a temporary shelter in the school gym. The gym was warm and dry, and it had room for many beds. Volunteers brought blankets, and neighbors shared food, so supplies were abundant by evening. Doctors from the clinic stopped by to check on the elderly guests. The mayor said the shelter would close once repairs were finished, and she asked residents to be patient because the recovery would be gradual.
blocks.question: 윗글의 temporary와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
blocks.explain: 시장이 수리가 끝나면 대피소를 닫겠다고 했으므로 temporary는 한시적인 것, 즉 short-term과 가깝습니다.
wrong: ① permanent는 반대 의미
②·④·⑤는 지문에 근거가 없음

blocks.label: 내용 일치 · 표준
blocks.question: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 고르시오. (윗글 참고)
choices: The shelter was set up in a school gym.
The shelter will stay open permanently.
The mayor asked residents to leave town.
The repairs had already been finished.
blocks.answer: ② The shelter was set up in a school gym.
blocks.explain: 첫 문장에서 the town set up a temporary shelter in the school gym이라고 했으므로 ②가 일치합니다.
wrong: ① 저녁에는 supplies were abundant라고 했음
③ 수리가 끝나면 닫는다고 함
④ 시장은 인내를 요청함

blocks.label: 문맥 속 어휘 · 심화
blocks.passage: Scientists must be (A)[accurate / careless] when they record measurements, because even a small error can change the result. When they (B)[compare / confuse] results from different experiments, they look for patterns that appear again and again. Only after a gradual build-up of evidence do they (C)[obtain / lose] a result they can trust.
blocks.question: (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks.explain: (A) 작은 오류가 결과를 바꾸므로 accurate. (B) 서로 다른 실험 결과에서 반복되는 패턴을 찾으려면 compare. (C) 증거가 쌓인 뒤에야 믿을 만한 결과를 얻으므로 obtain입니다.
wrong: ① (A) careless는 because 이하와 맞지 않음
② (B) confuse는 패턴을 찾는 것과 맞지 않음
③ (C) lose는 믿을 수 있는 결과와 반대

sections.en: Many cities have started to paint bus lanes red. The color makes the lane easy to spot, so drivers are less likely to enter it by mistake. Buses can then move faster, which shortens the trip for passengers. Red is also a popular color for sports cars. As travel times fall, more people may choose the bus over private cars. In this way, a simple coat of paint can change how a city moves.

blocks.label: 빈칸 추론 · 표준
blocks.passage: The new city rule bans cars from the old town on weekends. At first, shop owners feared that fewer customers would visit. Instead, the narrow streets filled with walkers, and many shops reported that people stayed longer and browsed more. The ban did not reduce visits; it changed how visitors ______.
blocks.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 차량이 금지되자 사람들이 더 오래 머물고 둘러보았다는 내용이 근거이므로, 방문 횟수가 아니라 방문하는 방식이 바뀌었다는 ①이 맞습니다.
wrong: ④ avoided the shops는 'browsed more'와 정반대

blocks.label: 빈칸 추론 · 쉬움
blocks.passage: A weather app can predict rain, but it cannot tell whether your own street will be wet. Forecasts describe wide areas, so small neighborhoods may stay dry while the rest of the city gets rain. An app is useful, but its forecast should be treated as ______ rather than a promise.
blocks.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks.explain: 예보는 넓은 지역을 설명하므로 작은 동네는 맞지 않을 수 있다고 했습니다. 따라서 약속(promise)이 아니라 가능성(likelihood)으로 받아들여야 합니다.
wrong: ① certainty는 promise와 비슷한 뜻이라 rather than 앞뒤 대비가 되지 않음

blocks.text: 체크 포인트: 문제를 푼 직후에 바로 기록해야 근거 문장을 기억합니다. 오답 선지가 왜 그럴듯해 보였는지도 함께 적어 두세요.

blocks.label: 내용 일치 · 표준
blocks.passage: Water in the desert village was scarce, so each family collected rain in large clay jars. During the dry months, the jars were checked daily, and neighbors shared water with anyone whose supply had run out. Children were taught early never to waste even a cup.
blocks.question: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 고르시오.
choices: Water was easy to find in the village.
Families stored rainwater in clay jars.
The jars were checked once a year.
Children were allowed to waste a cup.
blocks.answer: ② Families stored rainwater in clay jars.
blocks.explain: 각 가정이 큰 점토 항아리에 빗물을 모았다고 했으므로 ②가 일치합니다. 모르는 단어 scarce는 '부족한'이라는 뜻입니다.
wrong: ① scarce(부족한)를 모르면 반대로 고르기 쉬움
③ 항아리는 매일(daily) 확인함

②·⑤는 지문과 무관

blocks.label: 어법 선택 · 표준
blocks.passage: The students (A)[was / were] asked to hand in the reports that (B)[described / describing] their field trip, which (C)[was / were] held in May.
blocks.question: (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks.explain: (A) 주어 The students가 복수이므로 were. (B) 관계절의 동사가 필요하므로 described. (C) which의 선행사는 단수인 field trip이라서 was입니다.
wrong: ① (A) was는 복수 주어와 불일치
② (B) describing은 관계절의 동사 자리에 맞지 않음
③ (C) were는 단수 선행사 field trip과 불일치
⑤ (A)·(B)가 모두 틀림

blocks.label: 무관한 문장 · 표준
blocks.passage: Many cities have started to paint bus lanes red. ① The color makes the lane easy to spot, so drivers are less likely to enter it by mistake. ② Buses can then move faster, which shortens the trip for passengers. ③ Red is also a popular color for sports cars. ④ As travel times fall, more people may choose the bus over private cars. ⑤ In this way, a simple coat of paint can change how a city moves.
blocks.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오.
choices: The color makes the lane easy to spot, so drivers are less likely to enter it by mistake.
Buses can then move faster, which shortens the trip for passengers.
Red is also a popular color for sports cars.
As travel times fall, more people may choose the bus over private cars.
In this way, a simple coat of paint can change how a city moves.
blocks.answer: ③ Red is also a popular color for sports cars.
blocks.explain: 글은 붉은 버스 전용차로가 버스 운행을 빠르게 하는 효과를 다룹니다. ③은 스포츠카 색상 이야기라서 주제와 무관합니다. ④의 As travel times fall은 ②의 결과를 받아 이어집니다.
wrong: ①→②→④→⑤는 원인과 결과가 차례로 이어짐

sentences.en: Many cities have started to paint bus lanes red.
sentences.ko: 많은 도시가 버스 전용차로를 붉게 칠하기 시작했다.

sentences.en: ① The color makes the lane easy to spot, {{so|연결사}} drivers are less likely to enter it by mistake.
sentences.ko: ① 그 색은 차로를 눈에 잘 띄게 해서 운전자가 실수로 들어갈 가능성이 줄어든다.

sentences.en: ② Buses can {{then|연결사}} move faster, {{which|문법}} shortens the trip for passengers.
sentences.ko: ② 그러면 버스가 더 빨리 움직일 수 있고, 그것이 승객의 이동 시간을 줄여 준다.

sentences.en: ③ Red is {{also|연결사}} a popular color for sports cars.
sentences.ko: ③ 붉은색은 스포츠카에도 인기 있는 색이다.

sentences.en: ④ {{As|연결사}} travel times fall, more people may choose the bus over private cars.
sentences.ko: ④ 이동 시간이 줄어들면 더 많은 사람들이 자가용 대신 버스를 선택할 수 있다.

sentences.en: ⑤ {{In this way|연결사}}, a simple coat of paint can change how a city moves.
sentences.ko: ⑤ 이렇게 해서 간단한 페인트 한 겹이 도시가 움직이는 방식을 바꿀 수 있다.

blocks.note: ③은 붉은 버스 전용차로가 버스 운행에 미치는 효과라는 글 전체의 흐름에서 벗어나 스포츠카의 색을 이야기하므로 무관한 문장입니다. 나머지 문장은 '눈에 띔 → 빠른 운행 → 버스 이용 증가'로 인과가 이어집니다.
